_notes.about: Text of the StreetZim website (https://streetzim.web.app): free offline OpenStreetMap maps for the Kiwix app. Each language gets its own pages; people find them through search engines, so write naturally, as a native speaker would search and read.
_notes.html: Keep every HTML tag and attribute exactly as it is (<a href=...>, <strong>, & and the like); translate only the text between tags. Write characters directly (é, —, ’), not as entities, except & where the English has it.
_notes.placeholders: Keep {placeholders} as they are; move them where your grammar needs them.
_notes.this_language: Where the English says "in English" it means "in the language of this page": write it in your language about your language (French: "en français"). Keep "English" where it means English (the interface of the original map, English Wikipedia).
_notes.names: Kiwix, StreetZim, OpenStreetMap, Wikipedia, Wikidata, Overture, MapLibre, Copernicus, Sentinel-2, Internet Archive, GitHub, Google Play, App Store and torrent are names: keep them (in Latin letters, or the usual local spelling where one is common).
_notes.lang_name: The name of your language in your language (Deutsch, Français, 日本語).
_notes.labels: nav_*, finder_*, media_*, tier_all and gal_* are labels: links in the bar at the top, buttons, and captions under pictures (a caption is followed by " · " and a city's name). Keep them short. nav_maps and nav_langs also stand beside a count (91 Maps, 34 Languages).
_notes.credits: In credit_*, {author} and {licence} become links (a photographer's name, a licence's name such as CC BY-SA 4.0) and {place} the city's name in your language; {language} in gal_lang is a language's own name (العربية, 日本語).

meta_description: Free, fully offline OpenStreetMap maps for the Kiwix reader. Vector tiles, satellite imagery, 3D terrain, and Wikipedia info — works without an internet connection on iOS, Android, Mac, Windows, and Linux.
tagline: Fully offline OpenStreetMap maps for the Kiwix reader. Vector tiles, satellite imagery, 3D terrain, and Wikipedia — no internet connection required.
badge_mac_title: Kiwix on the Mac App Store
maps_intro: Pick a region below, install Kiwix, and open the .zim file. Hosted on the Internet Archive — each download includes a torrent.
maps_intro_lang: Pick a region below and download it in English: its map labels, search and Wikipedia are in English. Open the file in Kiwix, a free app; each map's page shows how, step by step.
feature_key_intro: Badges on each card show what's inside:
badge_photo_desc: find a place from a photo of a sign.
what_lead: StreetZim packages OpenStreetMap data — entire countries or continents — into a single ZIM file you can open in Kiwix. It works completely offline: no servers, no API calls, no internet required after the initial download.
what_p2: Unlike traditional offline map apps that ship raster tiles, StreetZim uses vector tiles rendered client-side with MapLibre GL JS. The result: smooth pan, zoom, rotation, and even 3D terrain — all from a single file on your device.
feat_vector_p: Smooth, sharp street-level maps with the OpenMapTiles schema, rendered live by MapLibre.
feat_sat_p: 10-meter resolution Sentinel-2 cloudless imagery for the entire mapped region.
feat_terrain_p: Hillshade and 3D elevation from the Copernicus GLO-30 global DEM.
feat_wiki_p: Tap any city, mountain, or landmark for its Wikipedia article and key facts.
feat_search_p: Search across millions of place names, streets, parks, peaks, airports, and POIs.
feat_offline_p: Just one .zim file. No accounts, no telemetry, no network. Open and go.
step1_p: Free reader for iOS, Android, Mac, Windows, and Linux. Get it at kiwix.org. On Windows and Linux, open maps in the Kiwix PWA for now: Kiwix Desktop 2.5 shows them blank, and its fix is only in the nightly builds so far.
step2_p: Pick a region above and download the .zim file (or grab the torrent for faster speeds).
step2_p_lang: Pick a region above and press its download button: you get the map in English, as one .zim file.
step3_p: Open the .zim file in the Kiwix app. That’s it — the map runs entirely offline.
sources_intro: StreetZim is built entirely from open data. Each map ZIM bundles content from these sources:
src_map: Map data: © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License (ODbL).
src_sat: Satellite imagery: EOxCloudless https://cloudless.eox.at by EOX IT Services GmbH (Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2021) — CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial use only.
src_elev: Elevation: Copernicus GLO-30 DEM — © DLR / Airbus, provided under the COPERNICUS programme by the European Union and ESA.
src_place: Place info: Wikidata (CC0) and Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0).

footer: StreetZim is an open source project. Source on GitHub. Maps hosted on the Internet Archive.

kg_h2: How to open the map in Kiwix
kg_android_1: Install Kiwix from Google Play. It is free.
kg_android_2: Download the map above. Your phone saves it in Downloads.
kg_android_3: Open Kiwix, go to its library and add the file you downloaded.
kg_ios_1: Install Kiwix from the App Store. It is free.
kg_ios_2: Download the map above. Safari saves it in the Files app, under Downloads.
kg_ios_3: Open Kiwix, go to its library and open the file from Downloads.
kg_mac_1: Install Kiwix from the Mac App Store, then open the downloaded file with it.
kg_pc_1: Open the Kiwix web app in your browser and choose the downloaded file. Kiwix Desktop 2.5 shows these maps blank; its fix is only in the nightly builds so far.
kg_offline: After that, the map works without an internet connection.
hero_h1: Maps that work without the internet
hero_apps: Opens in the free Kiwix app:
tour_lead: Everything in these clips runs from one file on the device. They were recorded with the internet connection cut; only the captions and the dots that mark each tap were added afterwards.
tour_photo_h: Photograph a sign, find the place
tour_photo_p: Take a picture of a street sign, a shop front or the address on a hotel key card, and the map looks for the place it names. The text is read on your device, in the script it is written in: here Ukrainian, Greek, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Chinese and English, side by side.
tour_photo_note: On the maps that carry this badge.
tour_zoom_h: From the whole city to one building
tour_zoom_p: Vector maps stay sharp at every zoom: fly from all of Kyiv down to a single building, then tilt and turn the map.
tour_drive_p: A route across Kyiv, worked out on the phone and followed turn by turn. Recorded with a simulated position; the middle of the trip plays at ten times the speed.
tour_terrain_p: Hillshade, 3D terrain and satellite imagery: the mountains above Tehran.
tour_signs_p: The same search in each script, on the map of the city where the sign stands.
tour_credits: The sign photos, the picture of the gate and the satellite imagery in these clips and screenshots are by others: see the credits and licences.
gallery_lead: Real screens from the maps, on a desktop and on a phone. Select one to see it full size, then flip through the rest.
gal_city: A whole city in one file
gal_place: Place card with photo and Wikipedia summary
gal_find: Find cafés, shops and more nearby
gal_route: A route worked out on the phone
langs_lead: Place names, search, directions, Wikipedia articles and the menus of the map itself, in the language you read. Right-to-left scripts included.
langs_step1_p: Pick it in the list below, or in the menu at the top of any page.
langs_step2_p: On your language's page, each map's main button downloads the map in that language, as one .zim file. This English page gives each map as it was built: place names in the local language, the interface and Wikipedia in English.
langs_step2_p_lang: On this page, each map's main button is “Download in English”: the map with its place names, search, Wikipedia and menus in English, as one .zim file. Where a map is not ready in English yet, its card says so.
langs_step3_p: Many maps can also be made in languages spoken there, such as Catalan for Iberia or Welsh for Britain and Ireland. Maps in other languages lists every language of every map and assembles the file in your browser.
langs_demo_note: The same map of Kyiv in Arabic, Hebrew, Hindi, Thai, Japanese and Chinese. A name with no translation stays as it is written locally.
langs_grid_note: The number is how many maps are ready in that language today.
